newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan BSPA buys 54,000T U.S. soybeans at tender.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan BSPA buys 54,000T U.S. soybeans at tender.

text.p: The Taichung division of Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association bought a 54,000-tonne shipment of U.S. soybeans from Continental at a tender on Tuesday, traders said.
The breakfast association's Taichung division consists of Sino Japan Feed Corp, Chia Hsin, Formosa Oilseed, Fwu Sow Grain and Tay Shan.
The shipment was bought on a cost-and-freight basis, traders said.

Traders expressed concern that Taiwan's outstanding soybean positions were growing dangerously large just as U.S. soybean futures were surging past eight year highs.
"If the futures rise too fast and too far, the Taiwan oilseed processing industry will be hurt," one Taipei trader said after the Taichung group's tender.
Traders estimated that Taiwan's outstanding positions had swelled to 17 million bushels.
Tuesday's big tender was the second in less than a week, as importers scrambled in the face of a CBOT futures squeeze and expectations of an unfavourable U.S. crop estimate on Tuesday.
An unaffiliated Taiwan competitor, the Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association Kaohsiung Division, bought 54,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans at a tender on Friday.
Traders said Taiwan's big soybean buyers ideally should have completed coverage through May by this time, but had yet to cover their February short positions.
"Buyers can be well protected if they cover through May, but they are still doing their February positions," a trader said.
